newsitem.title: GERMANY: Viag-BT group receive German mobile phone licence.
newsitem.headline: Viag-BT group receive German mobile phone licence.

text.p: The German government on Thursday said it has awarded the country's fourth mobile telephone licence to E2 Mobilfunk GmbH & Co KG, a company jointly owned by Viag AG and British Telecom Plc.
The company had previously received the concession on February 4, but final award had been delayed pending final examination.
Viag and BT were the only companies to apply for the licence.

The E2 licence is for operation of a digital mobile phone network based on the DCS 1800 standard. E-Plus Mobilfunk GmbH, owned by Veba AG, Thyssen AG and BellSouth Corp, operate the first DCS 1800 network.
There are also two networks based on the GSM standard: the D2 network owned by Mannesmann AG and AirTouch Communications, and the D1 network of Deutsche Telekom.
The Post and Telecommunications Ministry said details of the E2 licence conditions were published in the official Amtsblatt, Nr. 17 and the licence itself would be published in the Amtsblatt soon.
